Payment Scams

Wedding Photographer Scam UK: Verify Before You Book

Verify that the person, portfolio, contract and payment account all belong to the same photographer before paying a deposit.

By Alex Bacsa · Published 2026-06-10 · Updated 2026-08-01 · 3 min read

Quick answer: Before paying a photographer's deposit, confirm the person, portfolio, contract and payment account all belong to the same business — copied images and social profiles are exactly how impersonators operate. Reverse-image-search the portfolio, insist on a written contract naming the legal supplier, and pay by credit card where possible so Section 75 may cover a qualifying booking.
Key rule: verify through an official route you opened yourself, not the link, number, app, or payment details supplied by the suspicious message.

Being targeted right now? Do this

  1. Stop. Don’t pay, transfer money, or share passwords, PINs, or one-time codes.
  2. Contact your bank on the number on the back of your card if your money or details may be at risk.
  3. Use the right recovery route. Follow the payment, account and identity checklist; reporting differs in Scotland.

What can go wrong

A fraudster may invent a photography business or impersonate a real photographer using copied images, reviews and social profiles. A separate problem is a genuine supplier who later fails to attend or deliver the agreed work. Both cause loss, but only the first is necessarily fraud.

Warning signs

  • A portfolio whose images appear under unrelated names when reverse-searched.
  • Pressure to pay immediately or in full before a proper contract.
  • The payee name does not match the photographer or contracting business and cannot be explained.
  • Refusal to hold a video call, meeting or venue discussion.
  • Only selected highlight images are available and no coherent full gallery can be shown.
  • Payment is moved to an unexpected bank account or unprotected method.

Low price or a new business is not proof of fraud. Treat those as prompts for more verification, not as conclusions.

Verify the photographer

Reverse-image-search a selection of portfolio images. Ask to see complete galleries that demonstrate consistent work across a full event. Check independent reviews and speak through contact details found separately from the advert.

Ask for a written contract identifying the legal supplier, services, event date, delivery times, price, cancellation terms and image rights. If references are offered, verify that they are genuine rather than accepting screenshots.

Companies House only helps with entities that must register there; many photographers operate as sole traders. Companies House now verifies directors' identities but does not independently verify every other filed detail. A listing is one identity check, not proof of trustworthiness.

Pay with the protections understood

Section 75 may apply to a qualifying credit-card purchase where the cash price is more than £100 and not more than £30,000. A smaller deposit on the credit card can still cover the whole qualifying purchase, subject to the required debtor-creditor-supplier relationship.

Chargeback may be available for debit or credit card payments under card-scheme rules, usually with a time limit around 120 days. Neither route should be promised as automatic.

Wedding-insurance cover varies. Do not assume “supplier failure” is included; read the policy’s insured events, exclusions, excess and notification deadline. Venue deposits are the larger exposure and follow the same pattern; our wedding venue deposit scam guide covers the payment protection that applies.

If the service was not provided

Contact the supplier through verified details and set out the breach in writing. Contact the card issuer or insurer promptly where relevant. If the identity was fake or another photographer was impersonated, preserve the advert, portfolio, contract, messages and payment details and report it as fraud.

Report fraud at reportfraud.police.uk or on 0300 123 2040 in England, Wales or Northern Ireland; in Scotland, call Police Scotland on 101. For consumer advice, use the service for your nation: Citizens Advice in England and Wales on 0808 223 1133, Advice Direct Scotland in Scotland on 0808 800 9060, or Consumerline in Northern Ireland on 0300 123 6262.

Frequently asked questions

Does a Companies House record prove the photographer is genuine?

No. It may help match a registered company, but sole traders may not appear and Companies House does not validate every filed fact.

Can section 75 cover the whole booking if only the deposit was paid by credit card?

Potentially, yes, if the cash price and legal relationship satisfy section 75. It is not automatic.

Does wedding insurance always cover a photographer who fails?

No. Cover depends on the individual policy.

Fast checks

  • Pause before sending money or credentials
  • Verify with an official site, app, or number
  • Never share one-time passcodes
  • Be sceptical of bank transfer pressure
